head: 68c1bd00
gate: HTTP/3 buffered responses emit HEADERS, DATA and FIN in one QUIC packet when the owner is not multiplexing many responses at once
change: New adapter hook `sendCompleteResponse` on HandshakeServerSession uses `trySendResponseLiteral` to submit a whole buffered response in one packet, synthesizing content-length from the streaming body length when the caller's headers omit it. The concurrent engine uses it for `startResponseWithBody` only when the handler supplies the full body (fin, non-empty, no trailers, declared length matches) and `active <= 1`. The cleartext development runtime keeps the two-step path.
why_the_condition: Unconditionally using the literal path measured 72-76 us/request at batch=32, worse than the 48-49 us two-step baseline, because many in-flight responses lose packet coalescing and pay static-QPACK header encoding. Restricting it to the low-concurrency case keeps the packet-count win where it matters. Instrumentation showed the condition is true for about 70% of responses even in a 32-stream batch, since handlers finish quickly and the owner often sees one live slot while draining commands.

benchmark.workload: netz-only harness, zio event loop, HandshakeServer.serveConcurrentStreams + client startRequest/receiveNextResponse, GET -> 200 "ok"
benchmark.note: batch=32 is stable at about 39-40 us/request versus 48-49 before (about 20% better). batch=1 is noisy on this host (48-84 us across five runs) and improved versus the 75-93 us baseline in most samples; the machine was sharing CPU with an unrelated long build.

notes: Weft must call startResponseWithBody to reach this path; its current startResponse + writeData sequence is unchanged. The literal path finishes the request lifecycle itself, so the engine marks the slot finished and skips the separate body command.
